```sql
WITH base AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           ol.order_id,
           pv.id                     AS variant_id,
           sum(ol.quantity)          AS q,
           sum(ol.line_total_cents)  AS r
      FROM order_lines ol
      JOIN orders o            ON o.id = ol.order_id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY pv.product_id, ol.order_id, pv.id
),
per_order AS (
    SELECT product_id, order_id, sum(q) AS q, sum(r) AS r
      FROM base
     GROUP BY product_id, order_id
),
po AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           count(*)          AS order_count,
           sum(q)::bigint    AS quantity,
           sum(r)            AS revenue_cents
      FROM per_order
     GROUP BY product_id
),
pvc AS (
    SELECT product_id, count(*) AS variant_count
      FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id, variant_id FROM base) d
     GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       po.order_count,
       po.quantity,
       po.revenue_cents,
       pvc.variant_count
  FROM po
  JOIN pvc      ON pvc.product_id = po.product_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = po.product_id
 ORDER BY po.quantity DESC, po.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De twee `count(DISTINCT ...)` dwongen een brede sortering af op (p.id, o.id), inclusief alle productkolommen, en die liep naar schijf. Nu wordt eerst met smalle hash-aggregaties per (product, order, variant) en daarna per (product, order) gegroepeerd. Zo ontstaan de distinct-tellingen zonder grote sort, en worden de productkolommen pas aan het eind voor ~1750 rijen bijgevoegd; `quantity` wordt teruggecast naar `bigint` zodat het kolomtype gelijk blijft aan het origineel.
